sources_cited: DIA response to a request, dated 25 [month illegible] 1982 (memo reference S-26553/DB-2C)
key_claims: All six major resistance groups appear to have adequate modern assault weapons and ammunition but lack heavier weaponry.
Smaller groups in isolated provinces still suffer shortages of small arms and ammunition.
The Soviets cannot permanently seal Afghanistan's passes, owing to terrain, limited manpower, local hostility and resistance resourcefulness.
Resistance deficiencies include better surface-to-air missiles, anti-aircraft guns, heavy machine guns, antitank missiles and mines, man-pack mortars and tactical radios.
Soviets would respond to better-equipped resistance with higher-altitude bombing, escorted gunships and heat flares.
Even a 50,000-man Soviet increase would not significantly alter the situation; the insurgents would reassert control once forces moved on.
